s: It is frequently linked to Sanskrit roots such as hanu- or hana- (to strike, to accomplish) and, more convincingly, to the productive -esh suffix (from īśa/īśh, “lord, master”), seen in names like Rajesh or Ramesh. In this reading, Honesh can be glossed as “lord/master of prowess” or “the accomplished one,” with the initial Ho-/Hon- functioning as a contemporary phonetic adaptation rather than a strict classical morpheme.
